title: Know when an element connects
summary: connectedCallback runs when a custom element joins a document.
introduction: connectedCallback runs when a custom element joins a document. Your task: Write a message that describes your own component.
learningObjectives: Write a message that describes your own component.
Explain the example for know when an element connects

blocks.text: connectedCallback runs when a custom element joins a document. It may run again if that same element is removed and added later.
Run these HTML examples in this site's HTML playground. Each example defines its own custom element in a fresh page. No extra JavaScript library is needed.

blocks.code:
<visit-note></visit-note>
<script>
  class VisitNote extends HTMLElement {
    connectedCallback() { this.textContent = "I am on the page."; }
  }
  customElements.define("visit-note", VisitNote);
</script>
blocks.title: Know when an element connects

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `textContent` reads or replaces plain text inside an element. It does not interpret the supplied words as HTML.
`customElements.define` registers a hyphenated tag name with its class. Register a given name only once per document.
`connectedCallback` runs when the element joins the document. It can run again after a removal and reconnection.

blocks.text: The note writes its message once it is on the page.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Do not assume connection happens only once. Repeated connection should not duplicate timers or listeners.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Write a message that describes your own component.
